article_blocks.text: Strain Type: Sativa-dominant hybrid
Genetics: Original UK Cheese ( Exodus Cheese ) × Skunk #1
Breeder: Dready Seeds / Dready Bob
THC Content: 15–20%
CBD Content: medium
Terpene Profile: caryophyllene , limonene , myrcene
Primary Flavors: Pungent cheese, Skunk, spice, earth
Flowering Time (Indoor): 60–70 days
Outdoor Harvest Time: October
Indoor Yield: Medium to high
Outdoor Yield: Medium to high
Grow Difficulty: Moderate

Dready Cheese was created with a straightforward objective: preserve the unmistakable personality of authentic UK Cheese while making it available in a stable seed line. Dready Seeds approached that challenge by taking the original Cheese selection and breeding it with carefully maintained Skunk #1 genetics, then working the resulting population over multiple generations. The finished marijuana cultivar keeps the traits that made British Cheese famous—an extraordinarily penetrating odor, savory Skunk character, and a high that can shift dramatically with dosage—while adding enough consistency and vigor for indoor and outdoor cultivation.

Historical breeder specifications place THC at roughly 15–20%, flowering at 60–70 days, and production in the medium-to-high range. Dready Seeds describes its breeding program as focused on preserving important cannabis genetics while selecting for potency, yield, unusual terpene profiles, and medicinal potential. Dready Cheese fits that philosophy particularly well: it is less about novelty than about translating one of Britain’s most recognizable clone-only weed profiles into a worked seed variety.
Genetics and Lineage

The breeder-supported lineage of Dready Cheese is Original UK Cheese × Skunk #1. Dready Seeds began with the famous UK Cheese clone and selected a male from a closely held Skunk #1 population, breeding that male back into Cheese and continuing the project across multiple generations. Historical breeder material identifies the finished plant as sativa-dominant despite its relatively restrained height and its ability to develop a considerably heavier body stone at stronger doses.

Understanding the parentage requires remembering that UK Cheese itself is already rooted in Skunk #1. The original Cheese clone emerged in Britain from an unusually aromatic Skunk #1 selection, so Dready Cheese effectively reinforces those genetics with another carefully maintained Skunk male. Rather than radically changing the strain, the breeding strategy concentrates the traits that defined the original: aggressive odor, strong branching, robust flower formation, and a distinctive mix of cerebral uplift and later physical heaviness. Dready Seeds still treats Dready Cheese as an important building block; its current Northern Cheese combines Dready Cheese with an early-1990s Northern Lights #5 × Haze selection.
Effects and Experience

Dosage changes the character of Dready Cheese more noticeably than it does with many hybrids. Smaller amounts tend to emphasize the sativa side, producing a brighter mood, mental lift, and a sociable quality that can work well with music, conversation, outdoor activities, or relaxed creative projects. The effect is not necessarily razor-sharp or intensely stimulating. Instead, there is often a loose, cheerful quality that allows thoughts to wander without immediately producing the bodily heaviness expected from more sedating marijuana.

Increasing the dose brings out a different side. Breeder-era descriptions warn that heavier consumption can transform the uplifting opening into a strong, stony experience in which time seems to disappear and short-term memory becomes noticeably less reliable. Physical relaxation deepens, attention becomes less structured, and the cultivar becomes much better suited to an unplanned evening than to tasks requiring concentration. This two-stage progression is one of Dready Cheese’s defining features: it behaves like a functional, upbeat hybrid in moderation but can become substantially heavier when consumed aggressively.
Medical Benefits

Some medical cannabis consumers may find that progression useful because it offers a degree of control through dosage. A smaller serving may provide temporary mood elevation or help take the edge off everyday stress without immediately encouraging sleep, while a larger amount can produce more pronounced physical relaxation. Cultivars with this type of effect are sometimes selected by people dealing with tension, reduced appetite, minor discomfort, or difficulty unwinding after a demanding day.

Dready Seeds has increasingly focused its broader breeding program on medicinal cannabis and terpene selection, but Dready Cheese itself should not be treated as a clinically proven treatment for pain, anxiety, insomnia, depression, or another condition. Named weed strains can vary chemically between phenotypes and growers, and the original breeder’s description of “medium” CBD does not provide enough information to predict a therapeutic cannabinoid ratio. Anyone using cannabis medically should rely on the tested chemistry of the actual product and appropriate professional guidance rather than assuming the strain name guarantees a particular medical outcome.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Dready Cheese is not subtle. The aroma begins with the savory, sour funk associated with classic UK Cheese and expands into Skunk, earthy herbs, spice, and a slightly acrid fermentation-like quality as the flower is broken apart. Historical descriptions emphasize that the smell becomes extremely intense early in flowering—strong enough that indoor growers were advised to begin using effective carbon filtration only a couple of weeks into bloom. That level of odor is central to the cultivar’s identity rather than an incidental growing characteristic.

The flavor is similarly assertive. On inhalation, pungent cheese and Skunk tend to lead, followed by earthy spice and a lingering herbal sharpness. Unlike dessert cultivars that rely on obvious sugar, fruit, or vanilla associations, this strain belongs to an older savory branch of marijuana aroma. Dready Seeds did not publish a standardized terpene panel for the original release, so assigning a fixed dominant terpene would be misleading. Caryophyllene would be compatible with the spicy element and limonene with brighter accents, while myrcene could contribute earthy depth, but those possibilities should be confirmed through laboratory analysis of the individual harvest.
Growing Information

Dready Cheese develops long lateral branches that can be relatively thin compared with the weight they eventually carry. This makes physical support one of the most important cultivation considerations. The breeder specifically recommended netting to maximize production because unsupported branches may bend as the flowers gain mass. A screen can serve two purposes at once: spreading the canopy horizontally for better light exposure while providing a framework that supports flowering branches later in the cycle.

Flower development becomes increasingly attractive near maturity. Calyxes swell dramatically toward the end of bloom, giving the buds a chunky, exaggerated appearance while resin accumulates across the surface. Indoor flowering requires approximately 60–70 days. Outdoor specimens can reach around two meters according to historical breeder specifications, with harvesting completed by October in suitable climates. Production is categorized as medium to high rather than assigned a universal grams-per-square-meter number. That is the more realistic way to judge the cultivar because plant count, vegetative time, lighting, container size, training, and environment can change harvest weight substantially.

Temperature stability deserves unusual attention with this plant. Dready Seeds warned that significant differences between daytime and nighttime temperatures can trigger purple coloration accompanied by deficiency-like symptoms. Growers should therefore avoid assuming every color change is desirable pigmentation. In hydroponic systems, historical breeder notes described the plant as tolerating moderate-to-heavy feeding, with flowering electrical conductivity around 1.8 preferred and approximately 2.0 possible under suitable conditions. Odor management is essential indoors; few characteristics of Dready Cheese are as consistent as its ability to announce the presence of a flowering garden.
FAQ
What are the genetics of Dready Cheese?

Dready Cheese was bred from the Original UK Cheese clone and a carefully selected Skunk #1 male. Dready Seeds worked the cross over multiple generations with the goal of retaining the flavor and effects that made authentic UK Cheese famous.
Is Dready Cheese indica or sativa?

The breeder classifies it as a sativa-dominant indica-sativa hybrid. Its effects can initially feel uplifting and cerebral, although larger doses develop a noticeably heavier, stonier physical character.
What does Dready Cheese taste like?
Expect strong savory Cheese and Skunk flavors supported by earth, spice, herbs, and a sour fermented edge. Its fragrance is exceptionally powerful, particularly once flowering is underway.
How long does Dready Cheese take to flower?
Indoor flowering generally lasts about 60–70 days, or roughly nine to ten weeks. Outdoor plants are expected to finish by October in appropriate Northern Hemisphere climates.
How much THC is in Dready Cheese?

Historical Dready Seeds specifications list THC at approximately 15–20%. Modern examples may test differently because cannabinoid production is influenced by phenotype, cultivation, harvest maturity, storage, and laboratory methodology.
Final Thoughts on Dready Cheese

Dready Cheese is best understood as a preservation-minded interpretation of one of Britain’s defining cannabis cultivars. Dready Bob did not attempt to bury UK Cheese beneath unrelated dessert genetics or transform it into something unrecognizable. The project reinforced the original plant with selected Skunk #1 genetics and worked the offspring over multiple generations, keeping the aggressive aroma, savory flavor, and distinctive transition from cerebral uplift to heavier relaxation.

Its cultivation characteristics are equally recognizable. Long branches benefit from netting, calyxes swell dramatically late in flowering, yields can be substantial, and odor control becomes necessary remarkably early. A 60–70-day flowering cycle keeps the plant practical indoors, while roughly two-meter outdoor growth provides enough size for productive garden cultivation. For consumers and growers interested in genuine Cheese-family weed rather than strains carrying the word merely as a marketing reference, Dready Cheese remains a meaningful extension of the classic UK Cheese tradition.
